title: Levers: Load, Effort, And Distance
authorship: Independently developed for AbbyUsesAIThatCodes with AI assistance. Not an official PLTW product; no affiliation or endorsement is implied.
introduction: Work with the lever game linked by your teacher. Keep the game and this activity in separate tabs, or place them side by side when both are readable.

For a fresh setup, use Reset. For a continuing trial, keep the arrangement specified in the question. Hold the beam with Hold Level before editing values. A button labeled Release means the beam is already held.

Hide Math before making a prediction. If the button reads Show Math, the calculations are already hidden. Record your original prediction before using Release, then record what you observe in the separate result field. Keep your first prediction when you retry.
Use the game readouts for measurements. The drawings explain the arrangements; do not measure their printed or displayed lengths. They show the apparatus before the later balance pointer was added.

Here, balance means the two labeled masses have equal turning effects at level. Start each comparison held level and at rest, then release it. Do not use a momentary horizontal position during motion as your only evidence.
Use paper for the requested sketches. Keep your Part 1 work available for Part 2. Your teacher will provide the submission steps when the digital activity is ready.

blocks.text: The gold crate is the load; the teal hanging mass supplies the effort; the purple support is the fulcrum. Both objects apply downward forces. Mass uses grams (g); distance uses millimeters (mm).

blocks.alt: The complete apparatus: a load rests on the beam, an effort mass hangs from the opposite arm, and the fulcrum supports the pivot.

blocks.text: Move the purple Fulcrum by dragging it along the beam or opening Controls and changing Beam Position (mm) in the Fulcrum panel. Press Side View for this activity.

Beam Position is measured from the beam’s center: 0 mm is the center, negative is toward its marked left end, and positive is toward its right end. Arm Distances remain positive lengths measured from the Fulcrum.
